newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican judge orders two alleged EPR rebels held.
newsitem.headline: Mexican judge orders two alleged EPR rebels held.

text.p: A Mexican judge decided on Wednesday to keep in jail two men who were allegedly part of a guerrilla group that killed two policemen in a raid.

Tomas de Jesus Barranco and Rodolfo Tacuba Moreno were both seized in the small town of Tixtla in the state of Guerrero on Aug. 29, one day after a series of coordinated attacks by a new guerrilla group in two southern states.
They were jailed on charges of murder and terrorism and face sentences of up to 40 years on the terrorism charges.
In a review that is part of the Mexican legal process, Judge Angel Michel Sanchez decided to keep them behind bars and continue the case against them, court officials sai.
Two policemen were shot dead by rebels and two other policemen were injured in the fighting in Tixtla.
The lawyer for the two men said they were picked up by police in a cantina in Tixtla and had nothing to do with the new rebel force, called the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR).

A third person arested in the same town on the same day, 17-year-old Juan Jose Flores de la Cruz, was freed on Wednesday after being cleared of all charges, officials at a jail for minors in Chilpancingo said.
Troops continued to scour the area near Chilpancingo for members of the EPR on Wednesday, the Interior Ministry said in a statement released later in the day.
The Ministry said government troops wounded a man in the arm and leg after three people were seen running.
Official news agency Notimex reported on Wednesday that police in the state of Tabasco had detained a man under suspicion of having ties with the EPR.
It said this brought to five the number of people detained in that state who are suspected of having ties to the rebel group.
